transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because flying has started to feel a lot scarier than it should. Even just thinking about getting on a plane brings back this turbulence we had on my honeymoon flight, and I keep picturing it happening again. I know people fly safely every day, but it still really gets to me.
Did the fear of flying start right after your honeymoon flight?
Yes, pretty much. It started after that flight back from my honeymoon with the bad turbulence, and that was about two years and five months ago.
Do you experience similar fear or anxiety in situations other than flying?
Not really, no. I mean, I get normal nerves about things sometimes, but nothing like what happens with flying. That’s the main situation where it comes up.
Has your fear of flying interfered with your daily life or activities in any way?

A little, yes. I’m still doing fine with work and things at home, but I’ve started turning down trainings or conferences if I’d have to fly, even ones my supervisor thought would be good for me. And personally, it’s delayed plans too—like a trip to Florence I was really excited about.
How much distress does thinking about flying or actually flying cause you?

It causes me a fair amount of distress. Even just thinking about getting on a plane, I start picturing that turbulence from the honeymoon flight again. I know flying is safe and people do it all the time, but it still feels much scarier than it should.
Does seeing or hearing things that remind you of that honeymoon flight, like pictures of planes or news about turbulence, trigger your fear or anxiety?

Yes. If I’m looking at flights for a conference, or even if I hear a plane overhead, my chest tightens pretty quickly. I get this sudden rush of panic, like I need to shut the laptop or just get away from thinking about it.
Do you think the fear of flying would be less if you didn't keep remembering that specific honeymoon flight?

Probably, yes. I think that flight is a big part of it. When I think about flying now, my mind goes right back to that turbulence on the honeymoon flight, and then getting on a plane feels way scarier than I know it really is. I do know people fly safely every day, but that memory just makes it hard to feel calm about it.
Do you ever worry about flying when you're not thinking about that specific honeymoon flight?

Yes, I do. It’s not always a clear memory of that exact flight, but flying in general just feels way scarier than it should now. Even the idea of getting on a plane can make me tense, and then my mind usually ends up drifting back to that turbulence.
Is your fear of flying ever triggered by things unrelated to the memory of your honeymoon flight?

Yes, it can be. Like if I’m looking up flights for a work conference, or even just hear a plane go over, my chest tightens almost right away. I get this sudden panic feeling and I just want to close the laptop or get away from thinking about flying.
Is there ever a time when you feel anxious about flying without thinking about your honeymoon flight?

Yes. Sometimes it happens before I even think of that flight. Like if I’m looking at flights for a conference, or I hear a plane overhead, my chest tightens right away and I get this rush of panic. I just want to shut the laptop or get away from the thought.
Have you experienced any other symptoms like flashbacks, nightmares, or avoidance of things that remind you of anything else traumatic in your life, not just the honeymoon flight?

I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed flashbacks or nightmares about anything else traumatic. It mostly seems tied to flying, and I can’t think of another event that sets off those kinds of symptoms.
How long have you been experiencing significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to your fear of flying?
It’s been since that really turbulent flight coming back from my honeymoon… so about two years and five months now. That’s when it started affecting me in a noticeable way.
Do you believe that if you could overcome the memories and anxiety associated with the honeymoon flight, your fear of flying would significantly decrease or disappear?

I think it would help a lot, yes. The turbulence on that honeymoon flight is what my mind goes back to, and just the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture it again. I know flying is usually safe, but it still feels way scarier than it should. So if I could get past that memory and the anxiety tied to it, I think the fear would probably decrease a lot.
Do you think the anxiety you experience from the honeymoon flight is the main problem, or is it part of a broader set of issues related to that event?

I think the flying anxiety is the main problem. It’s like, ever since that honeymoon flight, just thinking about getting on a plane brings that turbulence back into my head. I know people fly safely all the time, but it still feels way scarier than it should.
Have you been experiencing these flying-related anxiety symptoms for more than three months?
Yes, definitely more than three months. It’s been going on since that turbulent flight coming back from my honeymoon, so… about two years and five months now.
Have you been avoiding flying or experiencing significant anxiety about flying for more than six months?
Yes. It’s been much longer than six months—since that turbulent flight back from my honeymoon, about two years and five months ago.
Have you been experiencing significant anxiety or fear related to flying for most days over the past six months?
Yes, it’s been there for a long time now. Ever since that turbulent flight coming back from my honeymoon—about two years and five months ago—I’ve had that fear around flying.
Do you believe the fear of flying would still be a problem for you if you didn't have the memory of the turbulent honeymoon flight?

I’m not sure it would be as much of a problem without that memory. The turbulence on that honeymoon flight is what I keep picturing, and now even the idea of getting on a plane feels way scarier than it should, even though I know people fly safely all the time.

Do you think the anxiety you experience from flying is related to the fear of the plane crashing or other accidents, or is it more about reliving the terrifying experience of the turbulent honeymoon flight?

It’s more about picturing that turbulent honeymoon flight again. I mean, part of me worries something could go wrong, but the main thing is that just thinking about getting on a plane brings that feeling back, even though I know people fly safely every day.
